topic: Changes in Materials Due to Temperature
key_concepts: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a material.
High temperature indicates hotness; low temperature indicates coldness.
Heating increases temperature; cooling decreases temperature.
Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
Some solids change into liquids when heated.
Melting is the process of changing solid into liquid.
Butter, ice cream, ice cubes, crayons, and candles can melt when heated.
Liquids can change into solids when cooled.
Freezing or solidification is the process of changing liquid into solid.
Freezing happens when a material reaches its freezing point.
Some melted materials can solidify in cold open spaces without a freezer.
